answer: A farm must hence either lie, which the nectar graph proves on replay, or recruit 16 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the spiral registry records each claim and the river audit publishes every slash. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 80% of the attester's bond. That is 32 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
